description: Qali-owned concise runtime bindings adapted from the locked upstream QA skills. These instructions are standalone; upstream paths are provenance only.

instructions.when: Create or refresh the shared project QA context.
workflow: Detect facts before asking.
Fill Product, Tech Stack, Test Stack, CI/CD, Environments, Quality Goals, Risk Areas, Team, and Conventions.
Validate completeness and provenance.
guardrails: Record current reality, not aspirations.
Do not invent unknown stack or product facts.

instructions.when: Bootstrap QA where no foundation exists.
workflow: Create project context.
Build risk-informed strategy.
Create the first bounded test plan.
guardrails: Skip artifacts that already exist.
Do not start automation before scope and expected behavior are approved.

instructions.when: Onboard into an existing team and test suite.
workflow: Confirm environment and access.
Audit coverage, reliability, CI, debt, and conventions.
Produce a progressive ramp with a first real test.
guardrails: Capture missing tribal knowledge.
Keep findings short, owned, and actionable.

instructions.when: Map one persona's end-to-end experience and friction.
workflow: Define one persona and journey.
Map phases, steps, touchpoints, goals, pain, and evidence.
Connect front-stage behavior to supporting systems and opportunities.
guardrails: Do not merge distinct personas.
Mark assumption-only journey steps as inferred.

instructions.when: Prioritize testing by business impact and probability.
workflow: Identify risks from journeys, incidents, dependencies, and change.
Score impact and probability from 1 to 5.
Map coverage and failure analysis to the resulting risk zone.
guardrails: Keep score evidence visible.
Reassess after incidents and material changes.

instructions.when: Define the durable quality approach and gates.
workflow: Read project context and risk matrix.
Choose test levels and environments by risk.
Define measurable gates, owners, and review triggers.
guardrails: Avoid tool-first strategy.
Every target needs a measurable signal and cadence.

instructions.when: Plan one sprint, feature, or release.
workflow: Decompose scope into observable scenarios.
Map every requirement to coverage and expose gaps.
Prioritize by risk and reserve explicit investigation buffer.
guardrails: Never hide unmapped requirements.
Do not schedule all available capacity.

instructions.when: Run time-boxed learning and bug discovery.
workflow: Write a target-resource-information charter.
Explore for 45 to 90 minutes using risk and boundary heuristics.
Debrief observations, evidence, questions, and follow-ups.
guardrails: An observation is not confirmed expected behavior.
Reproducible findings become regression candidates only after approval.

instructions.when: Explore a changing UI from a bounded natural-language goal.
workflow: Use seeded state, a pinned model, zero temperature, and a step budget.
Navigate through the accessibility tree.
Evaluate explicit positive and forbidden-state oracles outside the model.
guardrails: The model never grades itself.
Graduate stable critical flows to deterministic Playwright tests.

workflow: Start from an approved scenario.
Use isolated fixtures, user-facing locators, and web-first assertions.
Run type checks and the targeted suite with evidence on failure.
guardrails: Never use fixed sleeps.
Do not author tests from unapproved observed behavior.

instructions.when: Draft new tests from approved requirements or defect evidence.
workflow: Extract explicit requirements and flag inference.
Map risks, scenarios, and independent oracles.
Generate code only after coverage review, then verify imports, selectors, and execution.
guardrails: Code before coverage is forbidden.
Human review is required before generated tests merge.

instructions.when: Protect approved visual appearance with repeatable comparisons.
workflow: Choose critical surfaces and fixed viewports.
Freeze or mask dynamic content.
Store expected, actual, and diff artifacts for review.
guardrails: Never update baselines automatically.
Generate baselines in the same rendering environment used by CI.

instructions.when: Create deterministic, isolated, privacy-safe test data.
workflow: Use factories for mutable entities and fixtures for static references.
Seed randomness and time.
Clean up per test and verify idempotent shared seeds.
guardrails: Never copy production PII without irreversible anonymization.
Tests must not depend on shared mutable records.

instructions.when: Turn a vague defect into a deterministic minimal reproduction.
workflow: Capture exact environment, inputs, expected, actual, and frequency.
Reproduce, minimize one variable at a time, isolate, and capture evidence.
Write the regression test red before the fix and verify red-green-revert.
guardrails: Do not theorize before reproducing.
Do not weaken or disable the failing regression test.

instructions.when: Classify, deduplicate, and route evidence-backed failures.
workflow: Normalize volatile log data.
Fingerprint stable anchors deterministically.
Use model judgment only for explanation and routing, then request human approval.
guardrails: Never use an LLM as the deduplication source of truth.
Never auto-close or merge tickets.

instructions.when: Diagnose and stabilize one unreliable test.
workflow: Reproduce under repeated and parallel runs.
Classify timing, data, order, environment, clock, visual, or external-service causes.
Apply the cause-specific fix and prove repeated stability.
guardrails: Retries detect flakiness; they do not fix it.
Repairs must preserve intent and produce reviewable evidence.

instructions.when: Recover many selectors after one known UI refactor.
workflow: Compare old and new accessibility snapshots.
Infer each locator's intent and generate role-first unique candidates.
Apply only high-confidence candidates and validate the affected suite.
guardrails: Do not repair semantic behavior changes as selector drift.
All bulk changes require human review; never auto-merge.

instructions.when: Rewrite QA communication for a specific audience without changing facts.
workflow: Lead with failures, risk, or release decision.
Replace generic categories with sourced specifics.
Preserve numbers, severity, errors, and evidence links exactly.
guardrails: Never invent precision or impact.
Name unknown impact as unknown.
